title: #008. Bipartite Transportation Planning
subtitle: Route shipments from warehouses to stores respecting supply caps and meeting every store demand.
markdown:
# #008. Bipartite Transportation Planning

<!-- section:scenario -->
A distribution network connects $S$ warehouses ($i = 0, \dots, S-1$) with available stock `supplies[i]` to $D$ retail stores ($j = 0, \dots, D-1$) requiring at least `demands[j]` units.

Shipping 1 unit from warehouse $i$ to store $j$ costs `unitCosts[i][j]`. Choose continuous non-negative shipping flows `shipments[i][j] >= 0` to **minimize total freight cost** without exceeding any warehouse supply while satisfying every store demand.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P008Input`)**:
  - `supplies: number[]` — available capacity at each warehouse $i$
  - `demands: number[]` — required demand at each store $j$
  - `unitCosts: number[][]` — shipping cost per unit from $i$ to $j$
- **Output (`P008Output`)**:
  - `shipments: number[][]` — $S \times D$ matrix of non-negative shipments
  - `totalCost: number` — minimized total freight cost

<!-- section:example -->
In Case 1 (`supplies = [60, 80]`, `demands = [40, 50, 40]`, `unitCosts = [[4, 6, 8], [5, 3, 2]]`):

- Warehouse 1 (`80` units) is cheapest for Stores 2 and 1, so it sends `40` to Store 2 (`cost 80`) and `40` to Store 1 (`cost 120`).
- Warehouse 0 supplies all `40` to Store 0 (`cost 160`) plus the remaining `10` for Store 1 (`cost 60`), reaching minimum cost **`420`** (leaving `10` surplus stock in Warehouse 0).

<!-- section:hint1 -->
The 2D continuous matrix `shipments[i][j] >= 0` is ready in the starter code:
- **Supply limits** (for every warehouse $i$): `sum(shipments[i]) <= supplies[i]`
- **Demand satisfaction** (for every store $j$): `sum(shipments.map((row) => row[j])) >= demands[j]`

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Minimize `sum_{i, j} unitCosts[i][j] * shipments[i][j]`! Notice that when all `supplies` and `demands` are integers, standard transportation LP solutions automatically land on integer vertices without needing integer variables.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x \ge 0} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{S-1} \sum_{j=0}^{D-1} c_{i,j} x_{i,j} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{D-1} x_{i,j} \le S_i && \forall i \in \{0, \dots, S-1\} \\
& \sum_{i=0}^{S-1} x_{i,j} \ge D_j && \forall j \in \{0, \dots, D-1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { shipments, totalCost }.
judge.m1: shipments must be an array with {p0} warehouse rows.
judge.m4: Store {p0} inbound shipment ({p1}) is below demand ({p2}).
judge.m5: Reported totalCost ({p0}) does not match computed freight cost ({p1}).
judge.m6: Valid shipping plan, but freight cost ({p0}) exceeds minimum ({p1}).
